title: GEM vs the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir: Do You Need Both?
excerpt: Grand Egyptian Museum vs Egyptian Museum: what moved to the GEM, what stays at Tahrir, 2026 ticket prices (EGP 1,830 vs 550) and guided GEM visits from €48.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

The two museums are not interchangeable. The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM), beside the pyramids at Giza, holds the complete Tutankhamun collection, more than 5,000 objects, and Khufu's boats. The 1902 Egyptian Museum in Tahrir keeps the Narmer Palette, the Psusennes treasure and Yuya and Thuya, in an old-fashioned, far quieter building. Short on days, choose the GEM; with two days in Cairo, see both. Either way, the royal mummies are at neither: they are at the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization (NMEC) in Fustat. Foreign adult admission is EGP 1,830 (about €31) at the GEM from 1 November 2026, and EGP 550 (about €9) at Tahrir, at EGP 60 to the euro on 8 November 2026.

Check the Grand Egyptian Museum’s official ticketing website for current admission, entry times and gallery access.

You have one museum day in Cairo and two Egyptian museums competing for it, and much of what you have read is out of date. Since the GEM's full opening in November 2025, Tutankhamun's gold mask no longer sits on Tahrir Square; the complete treasure moved to Giza. The century-old Egyptian Museum is still open, and no longer home to the famous gold. This post sets out what moved, what stayed and which museum fits your days. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is a shared-departure marketplace for Egyptian day tours and short tours, and we have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993. For the plan that combines the GEM with the pyramids, see the Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day.

Grand Egyptian Museum vs Egyptian Museum: the short answer

Neither museum replaces the other: Giza's new giant and Tahrir's 1902 original are Egypt's greatest hits versus its deep archive. The GEM is the blockbuster: the Tutankhamun collection, the Grand Staircase and Khufu's boats. The Egyptian Museum in Tahrir is the dense, atmospheric veteran, focused on what the GEM left behind. As of November 2026 both are open: with one day, choose the GEM; with two, do both.

What the Grand Egyptian Museum holds

The Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza was inaugurated on 1 November 2025 and opened to the public on 4 November, after a partial opening from October 2024. It is the largest museum in the world dedicated to a single civilisation. Twelve main galleries hold part of a collection of more than 100,000 artefacts. In the Tutankhamun galleries the complete burial collection, more than 5,000 objects including the gold mask, is displayed together for the first time. The Grand Staircase carries more than 60 monumental pieces, and the GEM also houses Khufu's boats, moved from the old Solar Boat Museum beside the Great Pyramid.

Plan three to five hours. Galleries open 9:00 to 18:00 and stay open to 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays; the last ticket is sold about an hour before closing. Tickets are sold online only, on the museum's official ticketing site, tickets.gem.eg. Prices rose on 1 November 2026: EGP 1,830 for foreign adults and EGP 920 for foreign students and children, according to the museum's board announcement as reported in the Egyptian press. Tickets are non-transferable and non-refundable. Flash, tripods, selfie sticks and drones are not allowed.

What is still at the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir

More than most travellers expect. The museum, formally the Museum of Egyptian Antiquities, opened in 1902 in a building by the French architect Marcel Dourgnon, and holds over 170,000 items. The Narmer Palette, the roughly 3100 BCE slate recording Egypt's unification, is still there, along with the treasure of Psusennes I from Tanis (a funerary mask and a silver sarcophagus), the mummies and gold-leaf cartonnage of Yuya and Thuya, a statue of King Djoser and the colossal statue of Amenhotep III and Queen Tiye. Because galleries are being re-lit and re-labelled, ask your guide what is on display on the day.

Three headline groups have gone. Tutankhamun's entire tomb collection now lives at the GEM. The 22 royal mummies (18 kings and 4 queens) were paraded to the NMEC in Fustat on 3 April 2021. Khufu's boats left the plateau for the GEM, not Tahrir.

The pink 1902 building is half the experience: a Belle Époque atrium, vintage wooden cases, a century of atmosphere. The ground floor has been re-lit and re-labelled, and the Ministry has described the museum's development as a priority, so expect the odd gallery to be in transition. It is also quiet: one report counted roughly 200 to 300 visitors on a recent day, against up to 18,000 at the GEM. Budget two to three hours. A foreign adult ticket is EGP 550 (about €9) on the Ministry's list, and one 2026 guide says the ticket office takes cards only. Sadat metro station sits directly below.

Recommendation: on a first visit, take the GEM; Tutankhamun alone justifies the trip to Giza. If you love archaeology, early Egypt or old buildings, Tahrir rewards you. With two days, do both, GEM first.

Do you need to visit both museums?

No: one well-chosen museum beats two rushed ones. But since the 2025 transfer the collections barely overlap, so the case for doubling up is stronger than ever. Match it to your trip:

  • One Cairo day: the GEM, which has the headline collection and the easiest pairing with a pyramids visit.
  • Two or more days: both, GEM first and Tahrir second for the contrast.
  • Early Egypt and archaeology: Tahrir, home of the Narmer Palette.
  • Families: the GEM's wide halls and clear storytelling suit children.
  • Tight budget: Tahrir's foreign adult ticket (EGP 550) is under a third of the GEM's (EGP 1,830).

Details most guides miss

  • The royal mummies are at neither museum. They moved to the NMEC in Fustat in 2021, so allow a separate visit and check the current ticket price on the day.
  • Wednesdays and Saturdays are the GEM's late nights, open to 21:00. Weekends are very busy with Egyptian visitors, so a late weekday slot can be roomier.
  • Buy GEM tickets only on the official site. The museum warns it is not responsible for tickets bought anywhere else.
  • The GEM's guided ticket is a group product. Its own guided tours are offered in Arabic or English only; a tour with your own guide uses standard admission.

The verdict: GEM or Tahrir?

The GEM owns the gold, Tahrir keeps the deep story, and neither replaces the other. Pick the GEM for a first Cairo day, add Tahrir when you have two, and save the mummies for the NMEC. faq.q: Should I visit the Grand Egyptian Museum or the Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: Choose the Grand Egyptian Museum for a first visit: the complete Tutankhamun collection, Khufu's boats and the modern galleries justify the trip to Giza. Choose Tahrir if you love early Egypt and archaeology or have seen the GEM before. With two or more days, do both: they share very little now.

faq.q: Where is Tutankhamun's gold mask now?
faq.a: In the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, with the rest of the burial collection in the dedicated Tutankhamun galleries, together for the first time. The king's mummy itself remains in his tomb in the Valley of the Kings, near Luxor.

faq.q: Is the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir still worth visiting?
faq.a: Yes. It remains open, and its strengths did not move: the Narmer Palette, the Psusennes treasure, Yuya and Thuya and a large archaeological collection, inside a listed 1902 building. Plan for depth, not the famous gold: the mask, the mummies and Khufu's boats are elsewhere now.

faq.q: Where are the royal mummies in Cairo?
faq.a: At the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization (NMEC) in Fustat, where 22 royal mummies moved in the Pharaohs' Golden Parade of 3 April 2021. They are not at the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir and not at the GEM. The NMEC combines easily with a day in Old Cairo.

faq.q: How much do the two museums cost?
faq.a: For foreign adults, the GEM costs EGP 1,830 (about €31) from 1 November 2026, and the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir EGP 550 (about €9). Both change periodically. On Sawa, the Secrets of the GEM tour includes GEM general admission, and the Giza Pyramids, Sphinx & GEM day includes both the plateau and the museum tickets.
